newsitem.title: UK: Conservative gains too good to give up - UK's Major.
newsitem.headline: Conservative gains too good to give up - UK's Major.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday the transformation of Britain achieved by his Conservative government was "too good to give up" by people voting for his Labour rivals in Thursday's election.
"No one can honestly question that the transformation in Britain has been anything less than an economic miracle. It's too good to give up," Major told the campaign's final press conference.
Major said if the Conservatives won the election, they would be able to take forward his belief in a classless society "where more of the have-nots are able to join the haves".
"It would be a tragedy if these opportunities were lost by the false atraction of a well-packaged marketing scam," Major said in reference to the Labour campaign.
He said Labour was a "coalition of interests whose sole purpose is the pursuit of power" and who would throw away Britain's economic success by embracing continental European-style social policies.
Major was speaking before travelling around London on a final campaign tour to win over wavering voters, who, he told an earlier BBC radio phone-in, still held the key to the election.
Polls, however, give Labour a commanding lead of around 20 points with the hours now ticking away to the election. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
